The front-desk agent on shade areas
The aim of this section is to explain what the desk expects

Companion Animal Travel Desk Shift Rules

This section keeps the desk steady, fast, and clear for every animal trip request that comes through Aurelia Skyways. Stay alert, keep the line moving, and do not let small errors pile up.

Every change to a booking, crate note, or service request must go into the desk ledger right away. Use plain language, keep the facts tight, and make sure the record matches what was said at the counter. If a traveler gives a new route, a cabin change, or a care note for the animal, pass it along without delay and make sure the next crew member can follow it. The department shares practical instructions with crews, so do not leave out details that affect handling, loading, or the traveler experience.

Keep the tone calm but direct. If a pet seems stressed, if papers look incomplete, or if the traveler is unsure about the process, slow the exchange just enough to get it right, then move on. Do not guess, do not promise what you cannot confirm, and do not leave a case sitting open when it needs action. If Liam Sato, Aya Berg, or any other traveler comes back with a correction, update the ledger at once and tell the next desk handoff what changed. Treat every note on an animal like it matters, because it does.

Protect the workspace and keep forms in order. Check that travel tags, carrier notes, and desk handoffs stay with the right file. If something is missing, flag it fast and bring it to the shift lead before it causes a delay.

If a case turns messy or a crew reply conflicts with the desk record, contact the shift lead or the operations desk right away.
